title: AI Use-Case Identification and Business Triage

questions.question: Which candidate should Stage 1 reject before ROI work begins?
options: A drafting task where reviewers accept some variation in wording
A contract review that requires expert judgment recoverable from text
A sensor pipeline that needs deterministic readings and zero output variance
A meeting summary that turns spoken language into a concise record
questions.explanation: stage1_llm_fit requires a language-shaped task, human judgment, and acceptable variance. A sensor calculation with zero-variance requirements is better served by a deterministic system.

questions.question: The Multi-step research agent has annual_volume=10,000 and calls_per_task=25. What does stage2_roi count for model usage?
options: 10,000 calls per year because one user task is one billed call
25 calls total because calls_per_task is only a latency setting
50,000 calls per year because the agent uses five stages
250,000 calls per year, so the token cost includes the 25-call loop multiplier
questions.explanation: stage2_roi computes total_calls as annual_volume multiplied by calls_per_task: 10,000*25 = 250,000. Ignoring that multiplier would understate the agent's operating cost.

questions.question: A green-tier UseCase has needs_dpia=True but no other risk flag. What effective tier does stage4_risk return?
options: AMBER, because a DPIA obligation upgrades a green tier
GREEN, because GDPR never affects the EU AI Act tier
RED, because any personal-data assessment is prohibited
The original tier unchanged, with a note only
questions.explanation: stage4_risk appends the DPIA note and changes GREEN to AMBER when personal data will be sent to an external API. It does not make the use case prohibited.

questions.question: For a UseCase with value=4, readiness=4, regulatory=True, data_not_ready=False, and an effective GREEN tier, what does score return?
options: readiness stays 4 and the use case is DEFER
readiness becomes 3 and the use case remains PILOT_NOW
readiness becomes 2 and the use case is DEPRIORITISE
regulatory=True forces RULED_OUT before scoring
questions.explanation: The regulatory overlay subtracts one from readiness, producing adjusted_readiness=3. Both value and adjusted readiness meet the pilot thresholds, and the stated GREEN tier permits the quick-win track.

questions.question: What pair does requalify_with_hard_read return for the Contract clause extractor survivor?
options: (False, False), because the shallow SME check remains authoritative
(True, False), because it adds a blocker but the survivor was never a quick win
(True, True), because the common-case smuggle adds a blocker to a former quick win
(False, True), because the hard read changes only the printed explanation
questions.explanation: The contract extractor has no shallow Stage 3 blockers and its ROI and tier qualify it as a quick win. HARD_CASE_FLAGS reopens the SME gate, so the result is reclassified and records that it was previously quick-win.

questions.question: What evidence is missing when a Stage 3 SME gate passes common examples but not the long tail?
options: A larger model name and a higher temperature setting
A stage-5 score before any feasibility work is done
A vendor comparison that ignores the task's exception distribution
An evaluation set and SME labels that include the unusual cases the production queue will contain
questions.explanation: The common-case smuggle hides the hard distribution. The gate is only meaningful when the SME can label and the evaluation set covers unusual, multi-hop, or otherwise difficult inputs.
